context: A police officer briefs a uni reporter about road incidents
purpose: Teach: 重量/有害/摂取/歩行/多発/救助/連発/体感

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 本市の交差点、最近事故が多発しています。
lines.en: We've been seeing a spike in accidents at city intersections lately.
lines.style: Professional, steady opener. Measured delivery, no alarm. Straightforward statement of fact, like he's briefed others on this before.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 歩行者と重量車両の接触が中心ですか。
lines.en: Are most of those involving pedestrians and heavy vehicles?
lines.style: Respectful inquiry, leaning forward slightly. Genuine curiosity—he's note-taking mentally. Thoughtful pause before the question, like he's choosing his words carefully.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: はい。有害排気の摂取被害も懸念です。
lines.en: Yes. And there's also the concern of harmful exhaust exposure for people nearby.
lines.style: Even-keeled, clinical. Matter-of-fact listing of facts. No dramatization. The tone of someone used to reporting details that matter.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 救助は、消防と連発で出動する形ですか。
lines.en: So you coordinate with the fire department on every call?
lines.style: Clarifying follow-up, genuine interest in process. Soft and unassuming—not challenging, just confirming. The rhythm of someone taking notes.

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: おっしゃる通り。体感では、夕方の発生が一番多いです。
lines.en: That's right. From what we've observed on the ground, most incidents cluster in the early evening hours.
lines.style: Conversational shift—slightly warmer, more direct. He's settling into the rhythm of the interview. Confident in the data he's sharing.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 記事に反映させていただきます。
lines.en: I'll make sure to include that in the piece.
lines.style: Respectful closing. Quiet gratitude beneath the words. Ren acknowledging what he's learned, already mentally drafting.
